All of the research questions posed by this memo are really important. 

## Implications of the Financialization for Political Organizing

Financialization means that the owners have:

1. Different contacts with the state (connection to Daniel's memo)

    a. levels (connection to Lisa's memo)
    b. institutions (e.g., the SEC)
    
2. Deep pockets 

    a. Pro: suggests liability as a strategy/policy instrument
    b. Con: greater power in many venues via lawyers, experts, and money in politics (connection to Lev and Brian's memos)
    
3. Less concern for particular assets, only returns 
   
   a. Not place-based (connection to Jacob's memo)
        - hard to control via location-bound politics (again, see Lisa's memo)
        - not as powerful locally (unlike timber barons or other dominant local businesses/employers that control the local party machine)
   b. Don't mind shifting modes of production (private equity doesn't care if they are profiting from cutting trees or not cutting trees, whereas vertically-integrated )
